title: HTTPClient data race on lastResponseMetadata under concurrent use
description: client.go:243 and :275 write c.lastResponseMetadata unguarded on every operation. Sharing one HTTPClient, or one ScriptRunner wrapping it, across goroutines races. Confirmed with -race over 8 concurrent RunSource calls. Does not affect the CLI (single run) or gql.each (single-threaded VM); it hits embedders running several sessions off one runner. Guard the field and document that LastResponseMetadata is only meaningful for serial use.
close_reason: Closed

title: ScriptRunner WithReadOnly is bypassable: classify operations by parsed document, not helper name
description: gql.query("mutation Evil { deleteEverything { ok } }") is classified as a query because RequestInfo.Type comes from which JS helper was called, not from the document. A read-only runner sends the mutation to the server. Verified against a live httptest server. Fix: parse the document with gqlparser and derive the kind; also export the validator for consumers.
acceptance_criteria: A read-only runner blocks a mutation document passed to gql.query; RequestInfo.Type reports the document's real kind in hooks; exported RequireOperationKind rejects mismatched documents; no-option runners keep current behavior for unparseable documents.
close_reason: Closed

title: Make ScriptRunner safe to embed as a library (options, ctx interrupt, hooks, policy)
description:
Consumer embedding ScriptRunner to let an AI agent author ad-hoc GraphQL scripts. Current impl assumes (a) process stdout/stderr belong to the runner and (b) scripts terminate. Neither holds for LLM-written scripts inside a host program.

Add functional options to NewScriptRunner (additive, non-breaking):
1. WithStdout/WithStderr - console.log/error currently hardcoded to os.Stdout/os.Stderr (script_runner.go:33-36), corrupting a host's stdout JSON contract.
2. ctx-driven rt.Interrupt - ctx is only forwarded to client.Execute; nothing interrupts goja, so while(true){} hangs forever and context.WithTimeout is a no-op.
3. WithOnRequest/WithOnResponse - execution trace for the host.
4. WithReadOnly/WithApprover - per-dispatch mutation policy; source-text sniffing for 'mutation' is wrong in both directions.
5. WithMaxOperations - call budget.

Implementation: extract the 4 duplicated dispatch sites (gql.query, gql.mutation, both gql.request branches) into a single dispatch chokepoint so all policy/observability lives in one place.
design: Single (r *ScriptRunner) dispatch(ctx, info RequestInfo) chokepoint replaces 4 duplicated call sites. Interrupt goroutine must use defer close(done)+select to avoid leaking on non-cancelled runs. Distinguish cancellation via errors.As(*goja.InterruptedError). Copy RequestInfo.Variables before handing to host callbacks so a hook cannot mutate what gets sent. rt is per-call so cross-run interrupt is structurally impossible.
acceptance_criteria: NewScriptRunner(client) with no options behaves as before (existing tests pass unchanged); WithStdout/WithStderr capture console output with nothing to process stdio; while(true){} under 1s ctx returns within ~1s with an error distinguishable from a script throw; interrupt goroutine does not leak; WithOnRequest fires once per dispatch with correct Type for all 5 call forms; WithReadOnly blocks gql.mutation and both gql.request mutation forms, catchable in JS; WithApprover error blocks one op and lets later ops proceed; docs updated in README and both SKILL.md copies.
close_reason: Implemented: functional options (stdout/stderr, timeout, readOnly, approver, maxOperations, onRequest/onResponse), ctx-driven goja interrupt, single dispatch chokepoint, ProjectConfig.ResolveScript + NamedScript.MergeInput. 16 new tests, race-clean.

- HTTP-backed commands accept --insecure
- --insecure disables TLS certificate verification for requests
- Default behavior remains secure certificate verification
- Tests or integration coverage verify the flag affects client configuration
close_reason: Implemented --insecure flag for HTTP-backed commands, wired Config.Insecure into Resty TLS config and WebSocket dialer, added tests for TLS config and flag plumbing. Relevant insecure tests pass; full go test ./... currently fails in existing metadata flag tests unrelated to this change.

title: Expose timeout, retry, and fail-on-GraphQL-error controls
description: Why this issue exists: curl provides script-friendly reliability controls like max time, retries, and fail behavior. gqlcli has HTTP timeout plumbing but limited CLI exposure and needs explicit CI-friendly failure semantics for GraphQL errors.\n\nWhat needs to be done: Add CLI flags for request timeout, retry count/delay, and failing when a GraphQL response contains errors. Apply behavior consistently to operation and introspection requests where possible.
acceptance_criteria:
- HTTP commands accept --timeout with documented units/defaults
- HTTP commands support retry count and delay flags for transient failures
- A fail-on-GraphQL-errors flag exits non-zero when response.errors is present
- Tests cover timeout option propagation, retry behavior, and GraphQL error exit behavior
close_reason: Implemented timeout, retry, and fail-on-GraphQL-errors controls with tests; go test ./... passes

title: Add per-request --header/-H support across HTTP commands
description: Why this issue exists: gqlcli currently supports headers through .gqlcli.json environments, but curl users expect one-off per-request headers for auth, tenants, tracing, previews, and debugging.\n\nWhat needs to be done: Add repeatable --header/-H flags to query, mutation, batch, and schema/introspection commands (queries, mutations, types, describe). Merge these headers with environment headers, with CLI-provided headers taking precedence. Support KEY=VALUE syntax consistent with existing config add-env --header behavior.
acceptance_criteria:
- query, mutation, batch, queries, mutations, types, and describe accept repeatable --header/-H flags
- CLI headers override same-name environment headers
- Invalid header syntax returns a clear error
- Tests cover header merge precedence and at least one command path
close_reason: Implemented repeatable per-request --header/-H flags for HTTP commands, merging with environment headers with CLI precedence; added tests for precedence, invalid syntax, and command flag coverage.

title: LimitWriter for bounding captured script console output
description: WithStdout hands the host a raw io.Writer, so bounding output is left to them. A consumer truncates after capture, which does not bound memory: a script logging in a loop for its whole timeout balloons the buffer first. Provide a small capped writer so the common case is right by default.
close_reason: Closed

title: Document that script callbacks run on a single goroutine
description: A consumer added a mutex around WithOnRequest assuming gql.each dispatches from multiple goroutines. It does not: goja is single-threaded and gql.each is pure JS on the VM's goroutine (measured: concurrency 5 over 10 items = 10 calls, 1 goroutine). Document the guarantee on the callback options.
close_reason: Closed
